You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.02 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.15 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.01 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:
cond   vavg V  vmax V  vpp mV   tup s  Pload uW  vout_min vout_max ripple   startup  settled 
S1       2.24    2.25    26.2   0.269      15.2  ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL     FAIL    
S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       FAIL     FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL     FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 5 of 12.

RESULTS OF YOUR PREVIOUS ROUND:

Design 1 'SECE_Inductor_Out': failed the screen and was not tuned (topology 5109e08a95c1).

what this means:
- with the output fixed at 1.8 V, the net power delivered covers only 73 % of the load's need on S2 (heavy load), -214 % of the load's need on S4 (weak excitation) (best of the value presets tried)

REPEATED PROBLEM: your last three designs all show the same failure: too little power reaches the output on some conditions [underpower]. Change the part of the circuit responsible for it rather than its values.

BEST DESIGNS SO FAR (values already tuned):

*   Goal: Power a sensor-node RL from a piezo energy harvester.
    *   Constraints:
        *   `vout_min`: $V_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$
        *   `vout_max`: $V_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$
        *   `ripple`: $V_{pp} \le 0.02\text{ V}$
        *   `startup`: $t_{up} \le 0.15\text{ s}$
        *   `settled`: $dV \le 0.01\text{ V}$
    *   Piezo: $I_p \sin(2\pi f t)$, $C_p = 25\text{ nF}$, $R_{leak} = 20\text{ M}\Omega$.
    *   Operating Conditions: S1-S6 (various loads and excitations).
    *   Key failure of the best design so far (SSHI_FullBridge): **Ripple**. It's too high (e.g., 67 mV on S1, 92 mV on S2), while the target is $\le 20\text{ mV}$.

    *   Structure: Full bridge rectifier (D1-D4) + an L-S (Inductor-Switch) parallel to the piezo (SSHI-like).
    *   Tuned values: $C_{out} = 416\text{ nF}$.
    *   Ripple problem: The storage capacitor $C_{out}$ is too small to buffer the charge pulses, or the pulses are too large/infrequent.
    *   Wait, the current $C_{out}$ is $4.16 \times 10^{-7}\text{ F}$ ($0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$). The Reference Design used $2.2\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ and failed ripple too. To reduce ripple, I need a larger capacitor or a way to deliver current more continuously. However, the `C` limit is $47\text{ }\mu\text{F}$.

    *   The SSHI_FullBridge had excellent power delivery (passed $V_{avg}$ and $t_{up}$ on all conditions). The only failure was ripple.
    *   If $C_{out}$ was limited by the tuner, maybe it's because a larger $C_{out}$ increased $t_{up}$ too much? Let's check $t_{up}$: $t_{up}$ for SSHI was very fast (0.0438s to 0.124s), well within the 0.15s limit.
    *   This suggests that $C_{out}$ could be increased significantly to reduce ripple without violating the startup time.
    *   However, I am tasked with proposing *connectivity* (topologies). If the current topology (SSHI_FullBridge) is already providing enough power, but failing ripple, the tuner might have hit a limit or there's something about the current pulse delivery.

    *   The SSHI_FullBridge is essentially a synchronous switch that flips the piezo voltage (reducing the voltage across $C_p$ and thus increasing current flow into the rectifier).
    *   Can we improve the output side?
    *   The current setup is: Piezo $\to$ Full Bridge $\to$ $C_{out}$ $\to$ $R_L$.
    *   The ripple is caused by the discrete nature of the charge packets delivered by the bridge every half-cycle.
    *   To reduce ripple, I need to increase $C_{out}$. But wait, the tuner *already* tried values up to $4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$. If the best $C_{out}$ was $0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$, why? Maybe because for larger $C_{out}$, the voltage $V_{avg}$ took too long to reach 1.8V? No, the $t_{up}$ was already fine.
    *   Wait, the tuner might be balancing $V_{avg}$, $V_{max}$, and $V_{pp}$. If $C_{out}$ is too large, maybe $V_{avg}$ doesn't settle? No, $dV$ was "ok".

    *   Wait, let's look at the ripple: $V_{pp}$ is around 60-90 mV. The target is 20 mV. That's a factor of 3-4.
    *   If I can't just increase $C_{out}$, maybe I can smooth the output differently. But I only have resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, and switches.
    *   Wait, look at the SSHI structure:
        `D1 D pzp out DSCH`
        `D2 D pzn out DSCH`
        `D3 D 0 pzp DSCH`
        `D4 D 0 pzn DSCH`
        This is a standard full bridge.
        `L1 L pzp n1`
        `S1 S n1 pzn ctrl=G1`
        This creates an LC resonant circuit with the piezo capacitance to flip the voltage.

    *   What if I use a different rectifier? A half-bridge? No, that's less efficient.
    *   What if I use an LC filter at the output?
        Piezo $\to$ Bridge $\to$ L2 $\to$ $C_{out} \to R_L$.
        This would definitely reduce ripple.

    *   Structure: SSHI with an LC filter on the output.
    *   Components:
        *   SSHI part: $L_{flip}, S_{flip}, G_{sync}$
        *   Rectifier: Full bridge (4 x DSCH)
        *   Filter: $L_{filter}, C_{out}$
    *   Total components: $L_{flip}(1) + S_{flip}(1) + G_{sync}(1) + D_{bridge}(4) + L_{filter}(1) + C_{out}(1) + D_{zener}(1) = 9$ components. Well within the 16 limit.

    *   Is an LC filter better than just a larger $C_{out}$?
    *   The tuner should have found the optimal $C_{out}$. If $C_{out} = 4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ still yielded $>20\text{ mV}$ ripple, then an inductor is necessary.
    *   Let's check the ripple formula: $\Delta V \approx \frac{I_{load}}{f \cdot C}$.
    *   For S2: $R_L = 150\text{ k}\Omega$, $V_{out} \approx 2\text{ V}$, $I_{load} = 13.3\text{ }\mu\text{A}$. $f = 200\text{ Hz}$ (full bridge).
    *   $\Delta V \approx \frac{13.3 \times 10^{-6}}{200 \times 4.7 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 14\text{ mV}$.
    *   Wait, $4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ should be enough to keep ripple under 20 mV for S2. Why did the tuner pick $0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$?
    *   Maybe the pulses are very sharp (high peak current) and the ESR or some other effect is causing the ripple? Or maybe the tuner found that $0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ was the best balance for $t_{up}$ and $dV$?
    *   Actually, in the SSHI_FullBridge results: $t_{up}$ for S2 is 0.0638s. This is well below 0.15s. There's plenty of room to increase $C_{out}$.
    *   Wait! I can't change the values; the tuner does that. I only change the *connectivity*. If the tuner didn't pick a larger $C_{out}$, it's because it didn't help the score. The score is likely a weighted sum of all constraints. If ripple is the only failure, the tuner *should* have increased $C_{out}$ unless it hit the $4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ limit.
    *   Let's re-examine the results for SSHI_FullBridge: $C_1$ was $4.16 \times 10^{-7}\text{ F}$ ($0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$). This is far from $4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$.
    *   Why wouldn't the tuner increase $C_1$?
        Possible reason: As $C_1$ increases, the time it takes for $V_{out}$ to reach 1.8 V ($t_{up}$) increases.
        $t_{up} \approx \frac{C_{out} \cdot V_{out}}{I_{avg}}$.
        For S4 (weak excitation), $I_{avg}$ is very small.
        S4: $P_{load} = 3.91\text{ }\mu\text{W}$. $I_{avg} = P/V = 3.91\text{ }\mu\text{W} / 2\text{ V} = 1.95\text{ }\mu\text{A}$.
        $t_{up} \approx \frac{C_{out} \cdot 1.8}{1.95 \times 10^{-6}}$.
        If $C_{out} = 4.7\text{ }\mu\text{F}$, $t_{up} \approx \frac{4.7 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.8}{1.95 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 4.3\text{ seconds}$.
        **BINGO!** $t_{up}$ must be $\le 0.15\text{ s}$. This is why $C_{out}$ is kept small, which in turn causes the ripple to be too high.

    *   The conflict is: Large $C_{out}$ is needed for low ripple, but small $C_{out}$ is needed for fast startup.
    *   This is a classic power electronics problem. The solution is to have a way to charge the output capacitor quickly or to use a filter that doesn't impede the initial charging.
    *   An LC filter (L-C) can help. The inductor $L$ can provide a constant current to the output capacitor.
    *   Wait, an LC filter also slows down the startup (it limits the peak current).
    *   Actually, the best way to solve the ripple-startup trade-off is a "soft-start" or "bypass" circuit, but that's too complex for 16 components.
    *   Alternative: Use a synchronous rectifier (active rectifier) to reduce diode drops? No, the diode drops are already small (DSCH).
    *   Alternative: Use a boost converter? The SSHI is already a form of boost.
    *   Let's consider the "SECE" (Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction) or "SSHI" (Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor).
    *   The current SSHI_FullBridge is:
        Piezo $\to$ Bridge $\to$ $C_{out}$.
        The charge is delivered in bursts.
    *   What if we put the inductor *after* the rectifier?
        Piezo $\to$ Bridge $\to$ $L_{out} \to C_{out}$.
        This is a buck-like filter. It will smooth the current. But it also limits the charging current $I_{peak} \approx (V_{rect} - V_{out})/R_L$, where $R_L$ is the inductor's series resistance. This might make $t_{up}$ even worse.

    *   If $t_{up}$ is the limiting factor for $C_{out}$, we need a way to get the output to 1.8V quickly and *then* have a larger $C_{out}$ or a better filter.
    *   Wait, what if we use a smaller capacitor for startup and a larger one for ripple? (Impossible with these components).
    *   What if we use a Zener to clamp the voltage? (Already doing that with DZ33).
    *   Let's rethink. The current $V_{pp}$ is $\sim 80\text{ mV}$. We need $20\text{ mV}$.
    *   $V_{pp} \approx \frac{I_{load} \cdot \Delta t}{C_{out}}$. To reduce $V_{pp}$, we can:
        1.  Increase $C_{out}$ (but $t_{up}$ fails).
        2.  Decrease $\Delta t$ (the time between charge pulses).
        3.  Decrease $I_{load}$? (No, load is fixed).
    *   How to decrease $\Delta t$?
        The full bridge already pulses at $2 \times f_{piezo}$ ($200\text{ Hz}$).
        If we could pulse at a higher frequency... but the energy is only available at the peaks.

    *   Wait, what if we use a different topology like a charge pump?
        The SSHI is already very efficient. The problem is specifically the ripple vs. startup trade-off.
    *   Let's look at the SECE (Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction) topology.
        SECE usually uses a switch and an inductor to extract the charge at the peak and dump it into the rectifier.
        Standard SECE:
        1. Piezo charges the internal capacitance $C_p$.
        2. At peak, a switch closes, and the charge flows through an inductor $L$ and a diode $D$ into $C_{out}$.
        This creates a more controlled current pulse.

    *   Let's try a modified SECE:
        Piezo (pzp, pzn) $\to$ Switch S1 (pzp to n1) $\to$ Inductor L1 (n1 to out) $\to$ Diode D1 (out to pzn)? No.
        Let's try:
        S1 (pzp, n1)
        L1 (n1, out)
        D1 (out, pzn)
        This is a basic SECE. But it only works for one half-cycle.
        For both half-cycles:
        S1 (pzp, n1), S2 (pzn, n1)
        L1 (n1, out)
        D1 (out, 0) -- no, that's not right.

        Let's try this:
        Full bridge rectifier (D1-D4) from pzp, pzn to out, 0.
        And then a separate SSHI-like circuit to flip the voltage. (This is what SSHI_FullBridge was).

    *   Is there any other way to reduce ripple?
        What if we use a larger inductor and a smaller capacitor?
        An LC filter: Bridge $\to L_{filter} \to C_{out}$.
        $V_{pp} \approx \frac{V_{in}}{2\pi^2 f L C}$? No, that's for a different case.
        For a current-fed capacitor, $V_{pp} \approx \frac{\Delta I \cdot L}{R}$? No.
        Actually, a large $L$ and small $C$ can act as a current source, which reduces ripple.
        Let's try the LC filter.

    *   SSHI_FullBridge had $t_{up} \approx 0.12\text{ s}$ for S4 with $C_{out} = 0.416\text{ }\mu\text{F}$.
    *   If we add an inductor $L_{filter} = 10\text{ mH}$ between the bridge and $C_{out}$:
        $I_{peak} \approx (V_{rect} - V_{out}) / R_{L,series}$.
        $R_{L,series}$ for $10\text{ mH}$ is $2 + 5 \times 10 = 52\text{ }\Omega$.
        $I_{peak} \approx (3.2\text{ V} - 1.8\text{ V}) / 52\text{ }\Omega \approx 27\text{ mA}$.
        This is *much* higher than the $1.95\text{ }\mu\text{A}$ average current.
        So the inductor won't significantly slow down the startup, but it *will* smooth the ripple.

    *   L1 (pzp, n1)
    *   S1 (n1, pzn)
    *   G1 SYNC (ton=..., phase=..., edges=both)
    *   D1 (pzp, out), D2 (pzn, out), D3 (0, pzp), D4 (0, pzn) (Full Bridge)
    *   L2 (out, n2) (Filter inductor)
    *   C1 (n2, 0) (Storage capacitor)
    *   RL (n2, 0) (Load)
    *   Dz (0, n2) (Zener clamp)

    Wait, the problem says RL is from "out" to 0.
    So:
    D1-D4: (pzp, out), (pzn, out), (0, pzp), (0, pzn)
    L2: (out, n2)
    C1: (n2, 0)
    RL: (n2, 0)
    Dz: (0, n2)
    This means "out" is now the node *before* the filter. This is fine, as long as the load RL is at the final node.
    Wait, the prompt says: "A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node 'out'".
    And: "the load RL from out to 0".
    This means the final node *must* be called "out".
    So:
    D1-D4: (pzp, n2), (pzn, n2), (0, pzp), (0, pzn)
    L2: (n2, out)
    C1: (out, 0)
    RL: (out, 0)
    Dz: (0, out)

    *   16 component limit:
        L1 (1), S1 (1), G1 (1), D1-D4 (4), L2 (1), C1 (1), Dz (1) = 9 components. (OK)
    *   $L$ series resistance: $2\text{ }\Omega + 5\text{ }\Omega/\text{mH}$.
        For $L = 10\text{ mH}$, $R_s = 52\text{ }\Omega$.
    *   Startup: With $L_2$, the current is limited. But since $L_2$ is small and $R_s$ is small, the peak current is still plenty to charge $C_{out}$ quickly.
    *   Ripple: $L_2$ and $C_{out}$ will form a low-pass filter, significantly reducing the ripple from the bridge.

    *   Let's refine the SSHI part. The SSHI_FullBridge used:
        L1: (pzp, n1), S1: (n1, pzn), G1: (ton=7.48e-05, phase=0.0641, edges=both).
        This worked well for power. I'll keep that.
    *   Now add the LC filter:
        D1: (pzp, n_rect), D2: (pzn, n_rect), D3: (0, pzp), D4: (0, pzn)
        L2: (n_rect, out)
        C1: (out, 0)
        Dz: (0, out)
